reasoning_details.text:
Key contract: "use a server-issued, short-lived confirmation bound to the normalized request and current governed-input fingerprint for mutating or runtime-backed work" — SHORT-LIVED. And web: one-time token consumed once; hub dedup map entry removed at reap.

The TUI digest has NO short-lived component — the alias persists for ~37 days and blocks identical re-operations. TRD L2079 requires TUI to expose "focused reruns" same as CLI. A blocked rerun violates that. But is this a spine defect or intended dedup? The dedup's purpose is double-submission protection (double-click/Enter). Web achieves it with per-preparation one-time tokens (short-lived). TUI's digest is stable across preparations of identical intent → over-blocking. This looks like a genuine defect: legitimate reruns impossible from TUI until retention expiry, while the same flow works from web (new token each time) — violating cross-adapter parity AND "rerun" requirements.

Wait, actually let me double check the web path again: does a NEW prepare produce a NEW token? security.go:448-451 confirmationDedupKey = sha256(sessionID + NUL + token); token minted per prepare in preparation store with TTL 2 min. So yes, each fresh prepare → new token → different dedup key. After completion, re-prepare → new token → accept proceeds (alias unique). Web rerun WORKS.

TUI rerun BLOCKED (same canonical+fingerprint). Also note the TUI Existing card says lifecycle as state — for failed prior run it'd show "failed" state card, confusing.

Hmm, but wait — maybe TUI re-prepare produces different fingerprint because review.md etc change... For smoke-start rerun after failure: governed inputs unchanged (smoke evidence not hashed) → same digest. Blocked. For execute-start next task: Task field — does TUI set req.Task? If user selects task, Task differs → different canonical → OK. If empty (auto-next), blocked. For study-start resume vs start differ by Kind.

Also QA-start: .run-state.json IS hashed for QA kinds → changes after each QA run → different fingerprint → rerun allowed. Interesting — QA ops self-unblock via governed inputs. Smoke/review/execute don't include their mutable artifacts.

So the defect hits: repeated sprint-flow/stage/execute(auto)/review/smoke/verify starts from TUI when governed planning docs are unchanged between attempts. E.g., smoke fails due to transient harness flake; immediate rerun with identical parameters → "matching durable operation already exists" (lifecycle=failed). User must edit something or wait 37 days. That's an observable bad outcome contradicting CURRENT-CONTRACT rerun requirements (TRD L354-355, L436, L2079) and parity with web.

Severity: high-ish functional (blocks core workflow from TUI), confidence high on mechanics; medium-high overall. Actually let me verify there's no TUI-side nonce: tui/app.go:236 basis = CanonicalRequest + "\x00" + InputFingerprint. Confirmed no nonce/session.

But WAIT — maybe I should double-check whether repeat operations even reach AcceptOperation with the SAME confirmation object: beginOperation uses m.model.Confirmation which was set by ConfirmationMsg (fresh PrepareOperation). Yes fresh but deterministic.

And confirm ErrConflict is returned for duplicate ALIAS insert: sqlite.go:449-453 runError(CodeConflict,...) → matches ErrConflict via Is(Code==CodeConflict). Yes.

One more counter-check: does ResolveOperationAlias return the snapshot with Lifecycle — then AcceptOperation returns Existing with that lifecycle. TUI displays result card. So yes.

Now — is there any test asserting this behavior as INTENDED? Search tests for "already exists".

reasoning_details.text:
Both probes CONFIRMED:

**PROBE 1**: After a terminal (failed) run, re-accepting the same TUI-style digest returns `Existing=true` with the OLD run's lifecycle — the rerun is blocked. Combined with:
- TUI digest = sha256(canonical + NUL + fingerprint), no nonce/session component
- alias rows persist until run-row deletion (FullHistory 7d + TombstoneHistory 30d = 37 days default; only then FK cascade removes alias)
- web path uses per-preparation one-time tokens → fresh digest per retry → reruns work from web

So: identical repeat operations from the TUI are impossible for ~37 days whenever governed inputs are unchanged between attempts. This hits smoke retries, review reruns, execute auto-next, flow/stage re-runs. Violates CURRENT-CONTRACT: TRD L2079 ("TUI ... expose the same ... focused reruns ... as the CLI"), L436 ("expose readiness, progress, findings, artifact preview, rerun, cancellation, and recovery through shared CLI/TUI/web use cases"), sprint-32 reasoning "operation start retry-safe through confirmation-to-operation union" with short-lived confirmations.

Wait — one more counter-check on PROBE 1's reachability: does the TUI actually let you re-run the same operation? The confirmation flow: user triggers action → confirmationCmd → PrepareOperation → ConfirmationMsg stores m.model.Confirmation → user confirms → beginOperation. For a second attempt, PrepareOperation runs again → identical canonical+fingerprint → same digest → Existing card. Yes reachable. Also note: even while first op is STILL RUNNING, a duplicate submit shows "already exists" — that's the intended dedup. The defect is post-terminal blocking.

Severity assessment: high functional impact for TUI users (core workflow actions permanently blocked), no data corruption. I'd say severity High (major functional failure of a primary adapter), confidence High (proven by test).

Hmm wait, actually let me reconsider one thing: is `FinishOperation` deleting... no, aliases aren't touched at finish. And is there any OTHER unblocking mechanism — e.g., retention Compaction triggered by quota pressure could tombstone/delete earlier! Compact() runs on Accept when usage ≥80% hard quota. Default quota 512MiB — unlikely early. Also `run storage compact` CLI command maybe manual. So under normal operation: 37 days.

Also double-check FullHistory semantics: compaction cutoff = now - FullHistory/2 = 3.5d for compacting events (record_state compacted); tombstone at now-FullHistory=7d; deletion at now-(7d+30d)=37d. Alias cascade at deletion. So blocked ≥37 days unless quota pressure.

**PROBE 2**: Confirmed — cancelled inner runtime run with one pending coalesced progress event yields terminal outcome `persistence_degraded` (TerminalPersistenceLost) reason "durable event persistence failed", and returned error `persist progress omission: context canceled`. Correct behavior would be TerminalCancelled "runtime cancelled" per terminalOutcome mapping (errors.Is(parent.Err(), Canceled)).

Observable bad outcomes:
1. Durable journal mislabels routine cancellation as persistence failure → operators monitoring persistence_degraded terminals chase phantom storage faults; trust in the durability signal eroded.
2. Error surfaced to product/adapters is a persistence error text ("persist progress omission: context canceled") instead of clean cancellation — TUI/web show confusing failure copy.
3. Tier inconsistency: outer operation tier records cancelled; inner runtime tier records persistence_lost for the same user action.

Trigger/preconditions: controlledRuntime.StartRun where (a) ≥2 identical progress events land within ProgressCoalesceWindow (250ms) leaving progressOmitted>0, and (b) runCtx is already cancelled when StartRun returns (parent cancel, deadline, or acknowledged durable cancellation). Common with bursty tool-part updates from opencode sessions.

Root cause: run_control.go:305 flush uses `runCtx` (cancelled) instead of detached/bounded ctx; and :322 treats ANY flush failure as persistenceErr regardless of cause.

Also note asymmetry: manager-tier FinishOperation flush uses caller-provided (detached 30s) ctx — correct pattern. So fix is obvious: use context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), ...) for the trailing flush, or skip persistenceErr classification when errors.Is(appendErr, context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded) and parent cancelled.

Regression test: probe 2 asserts TerminalCancelled.

Now continue reviewing remaining areas before finalizing:

A. Manager-tier mid-run persistence failure → silent cancel → terminal mapping says cancelled/failed (never persistence_lost). Asymmetric with runtime tier; contradicts pack invariant §5 claim ("fail-closed ... ends in a persistence_lost terminal"). Let me verify by code reading again: controlOperation snapshot error → owned.cancel(); return. RecordOperationEvent append error → owned.cancel(). No persistence tracking in ownedDurableOperation. FinishOperation maps runErr: services return wrapped context.Canceled → cancelled. If service returns non-context error despite cancel → failed. Never persistence_lost. CONFIRMED by inspection. Should I empirically prove? Quick probe: repository.Close() then RecordOperationEvent → err → owned.cancel; then FinishOperation(ctx, id, state=failed?, runErr) — but caller passes its own state/runErr; the point stands by code. It's lower severity (mislabel only, plus silent swallow of tick diagnostics). Report as finding (medium/medium-low).

Actually wait — there IS one more twist: after owned.cancel() due to record failure, controlOperation exits silently; the operationCtx is dead; product drains. TUI finish passes r.State (from failedOperation: Is(Canceled)→cancelled) → TerminalCancelled. Web same. CLI doesn't record events. So journal: "cancelled". Meanwhile actual cause: db failure. And NO warning event persisted (append itself failing). At minimum the terminal should be persistence_lost like the runtime tier does. Finding stands.

B. FinishOperation omission-flush failure corrupts outcome mapping (flush error becomes runErr → failed/timed_out for successful ops). Edge case, medium-low confidence of real-world frequency, but concrete mislabel. Also note flush failure when runErr==nil AND state==complete → outcome failed "operation failed" though work succeeded. Counter-check: is that intended "flush failure = operation didn't fully commit = failed"? Defensible design choice honestly — the coalesced-count event failed to persist; marking succeeded would lose count info silently. But timed_out mapping (finish ctx 30s expiry → DeadlineExceeded) for a completed op is clearly misleading. Hmm, DeadlineExceeded arises only if proposeRunTerminalWithRetry... no wait, runErr set from appendErr during flush; if caller's finish ctx expired during flush retries (busy db >5s? appendRunEventWithRetry bounded 5s wall) — 30s ctx with multiple appends unlikely to exhaust... Actually waitRunControlRetry returns ctx.Err() if ctx done; Append honors ctx. Flush single append ≤5s retry window; ctx 30s. DeadlineExceeded only if caller passed <5s ctx or db hangs beyond. Low likelihood. I'll fold B into a minor mention within finding A? Or report as separate low finding. Doctrine says substantive findings only. B is speculative-ish; keep as non-issue/minor note.

C. QA fence heartbeat post-finish fails ErrStaleFence (attempt.outcome set). Sprint uses fence for writes during RunQA which completes BEFORE FinishOperation — fine. Post-cancel cleanup writes happen before finish — fine. Non-issue.

D. Web degraded mode: AcceptOperation returns ErrWebUnavailable — wait, where does ErrWebUnavailable COME FROM in AcceptOperation? App's manager never returns ErrWebUnavailable! web/operations.go:184 checks errors.Is(acceptErr, app.ErrWebUnavailable) — manager returns wrapped runcontrol errors (quota etc.), NOT ErrWebUnavailable. So when would degrade trigger? Only when h.ops doesn't implement DurableOperationManager (:181 type assertion). In serve, ops = webUseCases wrapping manager — need to check web_usecases implements the interface and forwards. If webUseCases embeds DurableOperations capability, assertion succeeds. Degradation branch (acceptErr==ErrWebUnavailable) appears DEAD CODE for real wiring — meaning: if accept fails for REAL reasons (e.g., QUOTA!), handler returns error → user blocked. That's fail-closed, fine. But hmm — quota-exceeded accept: soft-quota error is Retryable CodeQuota; user can't start ops until compaction. By design.

Wait, actually check web_usecases.go:444-449 mentioned in pack: "dashboard/web use cases return ErrWebUnavailable when the durable capability is absent". So maybe webUseCases.RunOperation/prepare wrap and the hub's h.ops is the useCases struct implementing DurableOperationManager only when durable != nil. Let me check quickly how hub gets ops and whether AcceptOperation errors get translated to ErrWebUnavailable anywhere... Search ErrWebUnavailable usages.

OK: webUseCases forwards Accept/Record/Finish and returns ErrWebUnavailable only when durable==nil (degraded wiring). So the hub's ErrWebUnavailable tolerance is for the nil-durable case. Real accept errors (quota, db closed) propagate → fail-closed. Fine.

Now let me verify a few remaining things:

1. **CLI smoke command** — sprint_commands.go:566 passes Stage:"smoke" in OperationRequest for smoke-start. sharedOperationRunner's smoke case doesn't use req.Stage. CLI flow: beginDurableCLICommand(OperationRequest{...}) then runs service directly. Fine.

2. **`durableCLICommand.Finish` state check order** — verified fine.

3. Now examine `run_control.go` controlledRuntime heartbeat cadence vs lease: tick 1s, heartbeat every ≥5s, lease 15s. If ONE Snapshot call blocks (sqlite busy timeout) — what's sqlite busy timeout? Check OpenSQLite pragmas. If a control tick blocks >15s without heartbeat (e.g., long Reconcile on big DB), lease could expire while work continues; another process's reconciliation could then mark stalled/interrupted? Reconcile uses grace 45s. Lease expiry alone doesn't terminalize. Then next successful heartbeat extends lease again (heartbeat verifies fence still current). If reconciliation cleared current_attempt_id in between, subsequent Append/Heartbeat fail stale-fence → persistenceErr → run dies with persistence_lost even though it was healthy but slow. That's inherited storage-tier behavior (dependency surface), not app spine defect. Skip.

4. **Reconcile called by EVERY control goroutine every 10s** — both tiers call global repository.Reconcile(ctx, probe, opts) — reconcile scans ALL runs workspace-wide each time per active run! With N concurrent inner runs, N goroutines each running full Reconcile every 10s on same SQLite → write contention (reconciliation_log inserts), busy errors under load → spurious cancel paths. Hmm — is that true? Reconcile writes reconciliation_log rows when decisions made; if nothing to do, maybe no writes but still scans + possibly PRAGMA/wal activity. Concurrent Reconcile from multiple goroutines on one *SQLiteRepository — database/sql pool serializes writes; SQLITE_BUSY handled? busy_timeout pragma presumably set. Performance/resource concern more than correctness; speculative without measurements. The doctrine says performance findings need concrete failure. A busy error here → setPersistenceErr → cancels a HEALTHY run (fail-closed over-trigger). But is there evidence of busy errors in tests? fault_test injects busy... For the spine, retryable ErrBusy is retried in append path but NOT in tick path: control goroutine treats any Snapshot/Heartbeat/Reconcile error as fatal (cancel). A transient SQLITE_BUSY on tick kills the run! appendRunEventWithRetry retries Busy/Unavailable ≤5s, but ticks don't retry at all — single busy → setPersistenceErr("poll durable run control") → persistence_lost. SQLite with WAL + busy_timeout makes transient busy rare but possible under concurrent writers (multiple CLI ops + serve in same workspace — explicitly supported scenario per TRD failure matrix "two CLI runs visible globally; a second supported server"). This amplifies finding A (silent cancel mislabeled) and adds: no retry tolerance on tick errors unlike appends. I'll fold into finding about tier asymmetry/silent cancellation.

Actually wait — check OpenSQLite pragmas for busy_timeout to gauge.

# Review report: `durable-operation-spine` (job `review-durable-operation-spine-correctness`)

Verified at frozen commits (`50d6f0d2` / workspace `ab12dc38`). Baseline `go test ./internal/app` green. Two probes were run via `go test -overlay` with files outside the repo — **no target file was created or modified by me**. Environment anomaly: `internal/sprint/qa.go|qa_test.go` were modified by something else mid-session (mtime 19:56; not my doing; left untouched; none of my findings involve them).

## Findings

### F1 — TUI reruns of identical operations are blocked until retention expiry (~37 days) — Severity: HIGH, Confidence: HIGH (probe-proven)
`tui/app.go:236-238` derives the accept digest as `sha256(CanonicalRequest + "\x00" + InputFingerprint)` — no nonce, session, or token. `AcceptOperation` maps an alias PK conflict to `Existing:true` (`durable_operations.go:106-112`; alias insert `runcontrol/sqlite.go:445-455`), and aliases are only removed by FK cascade when the run row is deleted — i.e., after `FullHistory+TombstoneHistory` = 7d+30d default (`retention.go:142-150`, `model.go:423-424`, schema `sqlite.go:306-314`; `expires_at` is never written; `Compact` never touches aliases; `ResolveOperationAlias` has no terminal filter).
Observable bad outcome (probe): accept → finish(failed) → re-accept the same request returns `Existing=true`, lifecycle `failed` — the TUI shows the static "matching durable operation already exists" card and cannot start. Since governed inputs for smoke/review/execute exclude their mutable artifacts (`operations.go:663-686`), fingerprints repeat verbatim between attempts, so routine smoke retries, review reruns, and auto-next executes are locked out of the TUI. The web adapter does not have this problem (`confirmationDedupKey` includes the one-time preparation token, `security.go:396-451`), QA ops self-unblock via hashed `.run-state.json`. Violates CURRENT-CONTRACT rerun parity (TRD L2079, L436) and sprint-32's retry-safe-per-short-lived-confirmation intent.
Regression test: accept→finish→accept same digest must yield a new run; fix = include a per-preparation nonce in the TUI digest (mirroring web).

### F2 — User cancellation of an inner runtime run is durably recorded as `persistence_degraded` — Severity: MEDIUM-HIGH, Confidence: HIGH (probe-proven)
The trailing coalesced-omission flush runs on the already-cancelled `runCtx` (`run_control.go:302-316`) instead of a detached bounded context; its failure unconditionally becomes `persistenceErr`, which skips `terminalOutcome` and proposes `TerminalPersistenceLost` (`run_control.go:322-331`; `Append` returns `ctx.Err()` at `sqlite.go:639-645`).
Probe: two identical tool-progress events 250ms-window-coalesced, parent cancelled → journal terminal `persistence_degraded` / "durable event persistence failed", returned error `persist progress omission: context canceled`. Routine Ctrl-C/deadline/durable-cancellation with pending omissions therefore pollutes the persistence-failure signal, misleads operators, and contradicts the outer tier which records `cancelled` for the same user action. Trigger is common (bursty tool-part updates within the 250ms window then cancellation).
Regression test: probe above must yield `TerminalCancelled`.

### F3 — Outer tier never records persistence loss mid-run; tick failures vanish silently — Severity: MEDIUM, Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH
`ownedDurableOperation` has no persistence tracking (`durable_operations.go:21-32`): `RecordOperationEvent` append failure just calls `owned.cancel()` (:208-216), and every `controlOperation` tick failure cancels and exits without surfacing or persisting anything (:235-261). `FinishOperation`'s mapping (:286-297) has no persistence branch, so such runs terminalize as `cancelled`/`failed` — never `persistence_degraded` — in contrast to the inner tier in the same package (`run_control.go:196-203,322-331`). Concretely reachable under hard-quota pressure, where non-reserved progress appends fail while reserved terminal/warning writes still succeed (`sqlite.go:620,713-720`): journal says "operation cancelled", truth is "storage full". Also contradicts the surface invariant that persistence loss ends in a `persistence_lost` terminal.
Regression test: fault-injected Append after start must produce `TerminalPersistenceLost` (or at minimum a persisted warning); today it produces `cancelled`.

### F4 — Web/TUI operation cancellation bypasses durable cancellation recording — Severity: LOW-MEDIUM, Confidence: HIGH (code)
Hub cancel only fires the local context cancel (`web/operations.go:347-374`); same for TUI (`tui/app.go:256`, copy at :265 claims "durable cancellation"). No `RequestCancellation` row/event is written for hub-owned operations, so `cancellation_state` stays `none`, no ownerless cancellation/ack events exist, and cross-process observers see the run active until the abrupt finish. TRD requires cancellation be "idempotent, durably recorded … arbitrated". The durable path exists (`app/run_commands.go:216`; handler fallback `operation_handlers.go:206-213`) but is reached only when the hub record is absent.

### F5 — Hub mutex held across acceptance I/O stalls all operations — Severity: LOW-MEDIUM, Confidence: MEDIUM
`startConfirmed` holds `h.mu` across token consume + `AcceptOperation` — including claim and the first append with its ≤5s Busy/Unavailable retry loop (`web/operations.go:151-218`; `run_control.go:345-356`). A slow or contended database (multi-process same-workspace access is a supported TRD scenario; busy_timeout is 5s) freezes `status`, `subscribe`, SSE fan-out, and every other start for the whole process.

### F6 — Promoted display keys can never persist; every message event gains a misleading "unsafe" omission — Severity: LOW, Confidence: HIGH (code)
`runtimeEventDraft` promotes `text/delta/content/title/native_type/line` "that the run timeline JS expects" (`run_control.go:450-453,478,521-529`), but the storage allowlist omits exactly those keys (`sanitize.go:10-21,36-50`), dropping them and tagging each event `unsafe event detail omitted`. Assistant/tool text is thus never durable despite the pipeline's stated purpose, and omission counts inflate with non-unsafe content — an internal contradiction between the two layers of this surface.

## Defended / non-issues
- Empty CLI digest writes no alias (`sqlite.go:445`) — no CLI dedup, consistent with synchronous one-shot commands.
- Alias-conflict `Existing` results carry caller ctx without ownership — safe because no adapter executes on `Existing`.
- `payloadHash` concatenation cannot collide (unique sorted keys, `k=v\x00` framing); byte-truncation rune-splits are mirrored storage-side and JSON-safe.
- QA fence heartbeat after finish correctly fails `ErrStaleFence` (attempt outcome set, `lifecycle.go:38-55`); pre-finish `WithoutCancel` heartbeats work (test-pinned).
- `FinishOperation` flush failure corrupting outcome to `timed_out` needs a <5s finish context; all wired callers pass ≥30s — unreachable today.
- Cross-manager finish nil-op success is unreachable in wired topologies (one manager per serve/TUI session/CLI command).
- Trust boundary holds end-to-end: fingerprint stripped and recomputed server-side at prepare and again before execution (`operations.go:215,376-409`), token consumption binds session+canonical+fingerprint (`security.go:413-437`), digests derive only from server-side data.
